root_cause.text: The net_device's sysfs parent (gadget device) is destroyed during unbind without reparenting the net_device, causing dangling sysfs symlinks because the net_device's lifecycle is not properly decoupled from the gadget device's destruction.
root_cause.evidence: CVE description states: "When the function unbinds, the parent device is destroyed, but the net_device survives, resulting in dangling sysfs symlinks". The patch introduces device_move() to reparent the net_device to /sys/devices/virtual during unbind and back to the gadget device on rebind, as seen in `gether_detach_gadget` and `gether_attach_gadget` / `gether_set_gadget` calls. Also the addition of `bind_count` ensures proper tracking to avoid double registration.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit d65e6b6e884a38360fc1cadf8ff31858151da57f
Author: Sascha Hauer <s.hauer@pengutronix.de>
Date:   Fri Nov 4 14:10:31 2022 +0100

    usb: gadget: f_ecm: Always set current gadget in ecm_bind()
    
    The gadget may change over bind/unbind cycles, so set it each time during
    bind, not only the first time. Without it we get a use-after-free with
    the following example:
    
    cd /sys/kernel/config/usb_gadget/; mkdir -p mygadget; cd mygadget
    mkdir -p configs/c.1/strings/0x409
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit moves the call to gether_set_gadget(ecm_opts->net, cdev->gadget) outside the 'if (!ecm_opts->bound)' block, so it is called every time ecm_bind() is invoked (lines 700-701 in the diff). This ensures that the net_device's associated gadget is always up-to-date, preventing use-after-free from a stale gadget pointer after bind/unbind cycles. The vulnerable construct (missing gadget update on subsequent binds) is therefore absent in the fixed code.
